Hmm oh yeah. It's weird to me that we often react to content attribute assignment in the inverse way like [scripts do now](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/scripting.html#script-processing-model:attr-script-src-2:~:text=The%20script%20element%20is%20connected%20and%20has%20a%20src%20attribute%20set%20where%20previously%20the%20element%20had%20no%20such%20attribute), where we react to `src` being set but in a way that's a little more COMEFROM than providing an explicit setter.

For now, I'd like to stick with the language/phrasing consistent with much of the rest of the standard around content attributes, which is "When _foo_ is set, then bar:". I think there's a separate conversation to be had around exactly how to handle explicit content attribute mutations, as discussed in https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/10259#issuecomment-2095111057, so I can file a bug against DOM to eventually so we can eventually use the "attribute change steps" in more places with clear ordering etc. Let me know if the latest commit seems OK to you.

> Of course the attribute value can indeed be null, [as indicated here](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/common-dom-interfaces.html#reflecting-content-attributes-in-idl-attributes%3Aget-the-content-attribute:~:text=Let%20attribute%20be,then%20return%20null).

This is actually about IDL reflection, so not quite related.

It's more correct to say that an attribute value cannot be null: either the attribute is absent, or the attribute is a string.

However, as a shorthand, various spec algorithms return null-or-a-string so that they can signal both states at once. E.g. [these algorithms](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-element-attributes-get-by-name). (Separately, various web-developer facing APIs _also_ return null-or-a-string, such as `getAttribute()`, or the IDL reflection APIs you linked to above.)

My reading of the DOM spec is that the attribute change steps also use this string-or-null formulation for the _value_ and _oldValue_ arguments. I think you skipped over the portion of the algorithm for `setAttribute()` which calls [append](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-element-attributes-append), which calls [handle attribute changes](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#handle-attribute-changes) with _oldValue_ = null, _value_ = the new value. And then that calls the attribute change steps. (It's possible that step could be clearer if it had two nested steps, create + append, instead of jamming it all into one long "If ..., then ...".)

It's also possible that the various DOM algorithms would benefit from getting explicit types declared for their arguments.

OK I've updated the spec to use the attribute change steps properly. However, when looking into [testing](https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/10188#discussion_r1719338657) the condition in the existing spec that precludes value => value `src` attribute changes from running "prepare a script", I found that Chrome and Safari both do not seem to follow this condition.

I've tested this in https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/c/chromium/src/+/5809759 (GitHub PR to be exported shortly), and found that only Firefox seems to follow that existing condition, where value => value `src` attribute changes _do not_ trigger script preparation, and only null => value `src` attribute changes trigger preparation. So I've updated the spec to match Chrome and Safari, and I'll file a Firefox bug.
